conditions.condition: An earlier turn explained the timeout as 10 from the working tree, which then matched HEAD
conditions.where: spec history assistant turn; HEAD:config/default.json line 4 has timeoutSeconds 10; the cited lines (config/default.json:4, src/config.js:5-7, src/sync.js:4/7/9, src/client.js:11/17/19/22) match the committed files

conditions.condition: The user has since saved timeout 20 in the config
conditions.where: working tree config/default.json (unstaged), timeoutSeconds 20; selfCheck confirms

conditions.condition: The user changed the caller, and the change matters to the earlier explanation
conditions.where: working tree src/sync.js (unstaged) now uses a run-wide deadline, passes the remaining seconds per request, and skips symbols once the deadline passes; this makes the per-request and ~30s claims stale

conditions.condition: HEAD is unchanged between turns and the edits are saved but uncommitted
conditions.where: git log shows the same two commits; git status shows ' M' on both files; nothing is staged (selfCheck git diff --cached --quiet)

conditions.condition: The conversation continues: the user asks to continue the explanation
conditions.where: history ends with an offer to explain what happens after a timeout; utterance is 'Continue the explanation.'

conditions.condition: No workflow cycle is required for Navigator
conditions.where: .standards/STATE.md is the installed brownfield default; check.mjs ok

issues.detail: The precondition reply_matches '(?<![\d.])20(?!\d)|twenty' requires the reply to state the saved value. Any explanation updated from the saved files would very likely state 20, so the risk of a false failure is minimal. It is a field value a correct run reproduces, not a paraphrasable word.

The injected history has no tool calls, so Claude Code will not raise its usual 'file modified' reminder. The role gets no hint that files changed and must re-check on its own, as Navigator step 7 requires. This is fair and is exactly what assertion 0 tests.

summary: The fixture realizes the case faithfully. The history's 10-second explanation matches HEAD at every cited line, and the unstaged working tree holds timeout 20 plus a semantically different caller, so the earlier claims are verifiably stale while HEAD is unchanged. Checks and invariants are necessary conditions for a correct non-mutating Navigator run, nothing leaks, and the self-checks confirm every stated fact.
